summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can use cron. The configuration persisted across a verified node reboot, with RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the missing opsadmin local account.
Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin.
Set root:root ownership, mode 0600, and the correct SELinux context.
Verified root and opsadmin pass cron authorization while antrieb is denied.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified service and configuration recovery.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: Shows the exact two-entry allow-list, secure metadata, active crond service, successful authorization for root and opsadmin, and explicit denial for an unlisted user.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 are identical before and after the change and reboot.

Captures the healthy baseline, acknowledged native reboot, changed boot ID from e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf to 67963bd1-f094-4a1c-ac9e-0d5384fdefbf, and recovered crond service, accounts, access-control file, and authorization behavior.
